scenes.heading: Ionic bonding
scenes.sub: Why salt is hard, brittle and conducts in water
scenes.say: Table salt, seashells and fertilisers are all ionic compounds. They form when metals hand electrons to non-metals. Let's see how, and why it matters.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.science: A metal transfers electrons to a non-metal, forming ions
scenes.breaks: atoms don't 'want' a full set; ions form because the whole process, including lattice packing, releases energy.
scenes.say: Imagine two mates swapping footy cards. Sodium has one spare card in its outer pile, and chlorine is one card short of a full set. Sodium hands it over. Sodium becomes a positive ion and chlorine becomes a negative ion. Opposite charges attract, and that's the ionic bond.

scenes.heading: Forming ions
scenes.say: Metals lose electrons to form positive ions, called cations. Non-metals gain electrons to form negative ions, called anions. The group tells you the charge: groups one, two and thirteen give plus one, two and three. Groups fifteen, sixteen and seventeen give minus three, two and one.

scenes.heading: Writing a formula
steps: Write both ions and their charges
Swap and drop the charge numbers
Simplify the ratio if you can
scenes.say: To write a formula, the charges must balance to zero. A handy shortcut is swap and drop: swap the charge numbers to become subscripts, then simplify if you can. Aluminium three plus and oxide two minus give A l two O three.
scenes.caption: To write a formula, the charges must balance to zero. A handy shortcut is swap and drop: swap the charge numbers to become subscripts, then simplify if you can. Al³⁺ and O²⁻ give Al₂O₃.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Write the formula of calcium phosphate.
lines: Lowest common multiple of 2 and 3 is 6
scenes.say: Calcium phosphate. The ions are calcium two plus and phosphate three minus. The lowest common multiple of two and three is six, so you need three calciums and two phosphates. Phosphate is a polyatomic ion, a locked box, so it goes in brackets.
scenes.caption: Calcium phosphate. The ions are Ca²⁺ and PO₄³⁻. The lowest common multiple of 2 and 3 is 6, so you need three calciums and two phosphates. Phosphate is a polyatomic ion, a locked box, so it goes in brackets: Ca₃(PO₄)₂.

scenes.heading: Naming
scenes.say: Name the cation first, then the anion. Ide means a single element, like chloride or oxide. Ate usually means the ion contains oxygen, like sulfate. For metals with more than one charge, use Roman numerals, like iron three chloride.
scenes.caption: Name the cation first, then the anion. -ide means a single element, like chloride or oxide. -ate usually means the ion contains oxygen, like sulfate. For metals with more than one charge, use Roman numerals, like iron(III) chloride.

scenes.heading: Does it conduct?
scenes.say: In a solid, the ions are locked in place in the lattice, so it doesn't conduct. Melt it or dissolve it and the ions can move and carry charge. Remember, it's moving ions, not electrons.

points: Metals lose e⁻, non-metals gain e⁻
Charges in a formula add to zero
Conducts only when molten or dissolved
scenes.say: Quick recap. Metals lose electrons and non-metals gain them. Opposite ions attract in a lattice. Charges in a formula add to zero. And ionic compounds conduct only when the ions can move. Now try the practice questions!
